title: Search Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and main trade-off of search fundamentals.
Apply search fundamentals to a small MongoDB data or operational scenario.
Verify the expected result, one edge case, and the relevant version/deployment assumption.

content.intro: Learn search fundamentals as part of MongoDB Search and Vector Search — Specialized. The lesson preserves the PDF subtopics, connects them to a practical MongoDB pattern, and ends with a verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Search Fundamentals is a specialist retrieval capability rather than a prerequisite for ordinary CRUD. Define the index and query deliberately, measure relevance on representative test cases, and verify the target deployment and version support the feature.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the behavior you want, identify the collection/document shape and access pattern involved, then select the smallest MongoDB operation that expresses the requirement. Check the chosen deployment docs and test representative queries or interrupted consumption before promising behavior.

content_blocks.code: db.articles.aggregate([{ $search: { index: "default", text: { query: "durable data", path: ["title", "body"] } } }, { $limit: 5 }]);
content_blocks.expected_output: In a supported Atlas Search deployment with a matching index, the pipeline returns up to five matching articles by search relevance.
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf displays this example as a reference and does not execute a MongoDB server or arbitrary driver code in the page. Run shell examples with mongosh, or driver examples in a separately configured Node.js/Python lab, against a disposable database. Verify installed server/driver versions and deployment feature availability first. Never place credentials in source files.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a dedicated training database and synthetic fixtures. Remove only objects created by this lesson or recreate the disposable database after confirming the target; do not run destructive/reset commands against production.

content_blocks.title: Environment and safety note
content_blocks.text: All examples are teaching references, not production-ready configuration. MongoDB Atlas-specific Search, Vector Search, monitoring, backup and automation features are marked as deployment-dependent. Server, driver, shell and managed-service capabilities differ; check the official documentation that matches your target.

content.task: Try it yourself: Create a tiny labeled retrieval dataset, define the required search/vector index, run representative queries, and evaluate relevance and metadata filters in the actual supported deployment. Submit your choice plus the expected result/evidence and one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate the key idea in Search Fundamentals.
Predict the result and state how you would verify it.
Name one boundary, risk or version/deployment assumption.
hints: First, explain what “Search Fundamentals” needs to accomplish in this scenario.
Write down the data shape, filter, expected output or operational evidence before running the example.
Test one normal case and one meaningful boundary/failure case; consult the matching official reference.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming specialist search/event features work everywhere
common_mistakes.why: Index types, resume behavior and service availability depend on the deployment and version.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the chosen deployment docs and test representative queries or interrupted consumption before promising behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a static reference result proves the environment will behave identically.
common_mistakes.why: MongoDB server, shell, driver, managed service and permissions can affect the available behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the target versions and privileges, run the smallest safe test, and keep expected and actual results side by side.
